articles.title: Un vecino de Egipto encuentra de casualidad en su terreno una estatua monumental del faraón Ramsés II
articles.standfirst: Khaled El-Shahat Khalil dio con un bloque de piedra grabado con jeroglíficos frente a su casa, en el delta del Nilo
articles.summary: Khaled El-Shahat Khalil dio con un bloque de piedra grabado con jeroglíficos frente a su casa, en el delta del Nilo
articles.body: Una jornada de trabajo cualquiera ha acabado en uno de los hallazgos arqueológicos del año en Egipto. Khaled El-Shahat Khalil, vecino de Behbeit El-Hagar, una aldea de la provincia de Gharbia, en el norte del delta del Nilo, arreglaba la parcela frente a su vivienda cuando se topó con un bloque de piedra cubierto de inscripciones. Lejos de sacarlo o venderlo, avisó de inmediato a las autoridades de antigüedades. Su llamada activó una excavación de urgencia a cargo del Consejo Supremo de Antigüedades. Los arqueólogos sacaron a la luz una enorme cabeza de piedra de 1,6 metros de altura que representa a Ramsés II con la doble corona del Alto y el Bajo Egipto, símbolo de la unificación del país. Según los expertos, la estatua completa, con su base, debió de alcanzar unos 8,5 metros. También apareció parte del pilar dorsal, donde figura grabado el nombre de Horus del faraón. Junto a ella, el equipo encontró una segunda estatua real, de unos 2,4 metros en la parte conservada, que probablemente representa al mismo monarca. Aunque le faltan las piernas y la base, su rostro, enmarcado por el tocado nemes, se mantiene en muy buen estado. Cerca de ambas piezas se halló además un bloque de granito rosa de 1,3 metros con dos títulos del rey: “rey del Alto y el Bajo Egipto” e “hijo de Ra”. La honradez del vecino no ha pasado desapercibida. El ministro de Turismo y Antigüedades, Sherif Fathy, viajó hasta la aldea junto al gobernador de Gharbia para homenajearlo en su propio terreno, rodeado de familiares y vecinos. Khalil y su esposa recibieron diplomas de reconocimiento y una peregrinación a La Meca. El ministro destacó que su aviso permitió estudiar el lugar con rigor científico y proteger las piezas. Behbeit El-Hagar es conocida por las ruinas de un gran templo dedicado a la diosa Isis. Las excavaciones continuarán y las autoridades no descartan nuevas sorpresas bajo el subsuelo.

articles.title: Karnataka NEET UG 2026: KEA allows candidates without seats to participate in stray vacancy round, check details
articles.summary: The Karnataka Examinations Authority (KEA) has extended the deadlines for the Karnataka National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test Undergraduate (NEET UG)
articles.body: The Karnataka Examinations Authority (KEA) has extended the deadlines for the Karnataka National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test Undergraduate (NEET UG) 2026 stray vacancy round for medical and dental seats.Candidates who do not currently hold a medical seat can also participate in the seat allotment process by paying the prescribed medical course fee, according to the updated information shared by KEA.The extension comes after several candidates requested an opportunity to participate in the stray vacancy round despite not holding a medical seat.Karnataka NEET UG 2026: Revised deadlinesCandidates seeking to participate in the stray vacancy round must complete the required steps within the revised timeline.According to the information provided by KEA, eligible candidates can pay the prescribed medical course fee by October 19, 2026, at 11 am.The deadline for filling in choices for seat allotment has also been extended to October 19, 2026, at 1 pm.Candidates should visit the official KEA website, cetonline.karnataka.gov.in, to check the latest instructions and updates regarding the counselling process.How to fill choices for Karnataka NEET UG 2026 stray vacancy roundCandidates participating in the stray vacancy round should enter their preferred medical or dental colleges and courses through the KEA counselling portal.They can follow these steps to submit their choices:Visit the official KEA website at cetonline.karnataka.gov.in.Open the UGNEET-2026 stray vacancy round option-entry link.Log in using the required credentials.Check the available medical and dental seats.Select the preferred colleges and courses.Arrange the choices in order of preference, placing the most preferred option first.Review the choices and make any necessary changes before submitting them.Submit the choices and save or print the confirmation page for future reference.Candidates must enter fresh choices for the stray vacancy round. Preferences submitted during earlier counselling rounds will not be considered.Candidates are advised to complete the fee payment and choice-filling process before the revised deadlines and regularly check the official KEA website for further updates.Get the latest Education News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Un arquitecto colombiano construye casas con seis toneladas de basura plástica en cinco días: los bloques encajan como piezas de Lego
articles.standfirst: Su empresa convierte bolsas, envases y botellas de champú en bloques encajables que permiten levantar una casa sin cemento ni albañiles expertos por menos de 7.000 dólares
articles.summary: Su empresa convierte bolsas, envases y botellas de champú en bloques encajables que permiten levantar una casa sin cemento ni albañiles expertos por menos de 7.000 dólares
articles.body: Seis toneladas de plástico y cinco días de trabajo. Es todo lo que se necesita para levantar una vivienda completa con el sistema ideado por Conceptos Plásticos, una empresa social fundada en Bogotá por el arquitecto Oscar Andrés Méndez y la ingeniera electrónica Isabel Cristina Gámez. Su propuesta transforma residuos plásticos en bloques que encajan entre sí como piezas de Lego, sin necesidad de cemento ni de mano de obra especializada. Los bloques se fabrican con bolsas, envases de alimentos y botellas de champú recuperados de recicladores y de la industria. Cada pieza contiene un 95% de plástico y pesa unos tres kilos, similar a un ladrillo convencional. Según los fundadores, el material es resistente a los terremotos, impermeable, ignífugo y aislante. Una casa tipo, con dos dormitorios, baño, salón, comedor y cocina, cuesta entre 4.000 y 7.000 dólares (de unos 4.000 a 6.000 euros), según National Geographic. Eso sí, el tejado, las ventanas y las instalaciones se añaden aparte. Méndez asegura que cada edificio podría durar más de 200 años. El proyecto dio el salto a África en 2017, cuando Aboubacar Kampo, entonces representante de UNICEF en Costa de Marfil, contactó con los fundadores. En Abiyán se generan cada día 288 toneladas de residuos plásticos y solo se recicla en torno al 5%. Esa basura obstruye los desagües, provoca aguas estancadas y favorece la propagación de la malaria. Fruto de esa alianza, en 2019 se puso la primera piedra de una fábrica en Abiyán que convierte el plástico recogido en ladrillos para construir aulas. El país necesita 15.000 nuevas clases para escolarizar a todos sus niños. La planta compra el material directamente a las recolectoras, en su mayoría mujeres que antes vendían lo que rescataban de los vertederos a precios irrisorios. Así, una sola idea ataca a la vez tres problemas: la contaminación, la falta de vivienda asequible y la escasez de escuelas, mientras genera empleo digno.

articles.body:
The alleged Cornell University gang rape has put a spotlight on programs and educational initiatives at colleges that address sexual violence.

But as Cornell’s president promises more student education on the issue after uproar on campus, the effectiveness of these efforts has come under nationwide scrutiny.

Cornell President Michael Kotlikoff said the university wants to change campus culture by investing more in prevention-focused programs, increasing existing education around the bystander effect and working with experts in national sexual violence prevention to strengthen strategies to address the issue on campus.

But current sexual violence prevention programs on campuses have shown they only do so much to reduce instances of assault.

Heather Kettrey, an associate professor at the department of sociology, anthropology and criminal justice at Clemson University, and her colleagues did a 2023 meta-analysis that found these trainings had a “much more substantial effect on knowledge and attitudes” regarding campus sexual assault than “they do on violence.”

“Typically, programs aim to change knowledge and attitudes as a means of preventing violence. Although campus sexual assault prevention programs do appear to improve knowledge and attitudes, there is not strong evidence that campus sexual assault programs are doing much to prevent violence,” she added.

Experts say the current prevention programs are often either easily forgotten or ignored by students, emphasizing more frequent trainings, lessons from a trusted person and greater emphasis on accountability from peers would be more impactful for students.

“Right now, a lot of people are learning this information once at the very beginning when they first get to college. Everyone’s a stranger, especially whoever’s teaching them this information …They don’t have trust in this person or rapport with this person, and so it’s not being contextualized, right? It’s not familiar to them, and a lot of people are just going to disregard,” said Omny Miranda Martone, founder and CEO of the Sexual Violence Prevention Association.

The programs need to not only cover consent and prevention strategies such as don’t walk home alone, Martone added, but also make clear the campus culture will not accept behaviors or comments that contribute to harmful situations and students will speak up against it.

“With regards to the Cornell case, if just one, just one of the people in that group chat had said ‘This is f—-d up, this is really f—-d up,’ then this might not have escalated as much as it did, right? It might not have gotten as big as it did. More people might not have joined … or it might not have gone on as long as it did without her getting the support that she hopefully is now receiving, right? But that didn’t happen. That’s not what happened. Instead, people egged them on, and anybody who was against it stayed sidelined,” Martone said.

The Campus Sexual Violence Elimination Act requires all higher education institutions receiving federal funding to implement sexual assault prevention programs with students, but the specifics are not universal.

Commonly, students will go through a one-time instructional session on sexual assault prevention, normally during orientation or through an online compliance program.

“What we want to do is see sustained attention to things like prevention training. So, these trainings can all be effective in letting students and the community know about resources that are there, about what they can do, for example, as a bystander, but we see these things be most effective when we have a higher dosage of exposure. So, we want to see these trainings repeated and offered in different times throughout the year, and not just as a one-time event,” said Jessica St. Germaine, executive director of consulting at RAINN, a group focused on sexual assault prevention and support for survivors.

The programming will talk about consent and the “bystander effect,” which is the failure of someone to act in emergency situations. Sexual assault bystander intervention teaches students about the responsibility to intervene if they see something and how to do so.

Despite years of this sort of training, a 2024 Higher Education Sexual Misconduct and Awareness survey found 1 in 17 undergraduate men and 1 in 5 undergraduate women experienced sexual assault during college, not accounting for the vast underreporting of the issue.

Fraternities commonly do their own sexual assault trainings, though many view frats as untrustworthy on the issue.

At Cornell, Jane Doe accused seven Chi Phi fraternity brothers of gang raping her after she was coerced into drugs and alcohol.

Many experts say to change the culture more broadly, consent education needs to happen well before a student reaches a college campus.

“The truth is that sexual violence prevention education is not a one time educational program. We know that the best approaches to prevention education start at a younger age. We can’t just expect somebody to show up at college and suddenly just understand consent, right? We need to be having these conversations about consent and healthy relationships and bodily autonomy and respect for others in age-appropriate ways,” said Tracey Vitchers, executive director of It’s on Us, a nonprofit dedicated to college sexual assault prevention.
